questions.set_intro: Imagine that a community music school is researching hobbies in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about learning a musical instrument.
questions.question: Which musical instrument would you most like to learn, and why?
questions.model_answer: I would most like to learn the piano. I already love the sound, and a digital piano fits in a small apartment much more easily than a drum set.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a community music school is researching hobbies in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about learning a musical instrument.
questions.question: Where can someone in your area take music lessons?
questions.model_answer: Most people in my area take lessons at a community music school. Others hire a private teacher who comes to their home once a week.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a community music school is researching hobbies in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about learning a musical instrument.
questions.question: What advice would you give an adult who wants to start learning an instrument, and why?
questions.model_answer: I would tell an adult to rent an instrument for one month and to book a weekly lesson, rather than only watching videos. A teacher can correct hand position early, before a bad habit settles in. I would also suggest practicing twenty minutes a day instead of two hours on Sunday. Short daily practice is easier to keep up, and it builds skill faster than one long session a week.

questions.question: Some people spend extra money on trips and hobbies, while others prefer to save all of it. Which do you think is better, and why? Give a reason and a short example.
questions.model_answer: I would rather spend some extra money on experiences than save every spare dollar. A trip, a class, or a day out with friends can give you memories and skills that remain after the money is gone. Last year a weekend ceramics class cost more than I had planned, but I still use what I learned, and I met people I now see often. Saving still matters. Rent, an emergency fund, and basic bills should come first. Once those are covered, though, a planned amount for experiences is better than watching a balance grow and never using it. The point is a limit, not a ban on spending. I would choose that amount before the month begins so the fun never crowds out the bills.
